'''Carla Molteni''' (born February 1966) is an Italian Professor of Physics at [[King's College London]]. She works on computer simulations of materials and [[biomolecule]]s.<ref name="CorsiniGreco2013">{{cite journal|last1=Corsini|first1=Niccolò R. C.|last2=Greco|first2=Andrea|last3=Hine|first3=Nicholas D. M.|last4=Molteni|first4=Carla|last5=Haynes|first5=Peter D.|title=Simulations of nanocrystals under pressure: Combining electronic enthalpy and linear-scaling density-functional theory|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=139|issue=8|year=2013|page=084117|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.4819132|pmid=24006984|arxiv=1305.5862
|bibcode=2013JChPh.139h4117C|s2cid=35313193}}</ref><ref name="MelisLummis2008">{{cite journal|last1=Melis|first1=Claudio|last2=Lummis|first2=Sarah C.R.|last3=Molteni|first3=Carla|title=Molecular Dynamics Simulations of GABA Binding to the GABAC Receptor: The Role of Arg104|journal=Biophysical Journal|volume=95|issue=9|year=2008|pages=4115–4123|issn=0006-3495|doi=10.1529/biophysj.107.127589|pmid=18641081 |pmc=2567930 |bibcode=2008BpJ....95.4115M}}</ref><ref name="MaRohlfing2010">{{cite journal|last1=Ma|first1=Yuchen|last2=Rohlfing|first2=Michael|last3=Molteni|first3=Carla|title=Modeling the Excited States of Biological Chromophores within Many Body Green's Function Theory|journal=Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation|volume=6|issue=1|year=2010|pages=257–265|issn=1549-9618|doi=10.1021/ct900528h|pmid= 26614336}} {{closed access}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Molteni studied physics at the [[University of Milan]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/nms/depts/physics/people/academicstaff/molteni.aspx|title=King's College London - Prof Carla Molteni|website=kcl.ac.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref> She remained there for her graduate studies.<ref name=":0" /> She was originally interested in particle physics, but became more fascinated by material science as she became aware of its impact in designing materials of the future.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/hr/diversity/meettheprofessors/nms/molteni.aspx|title=King's College London - Professor Carla Molteni|website=kcl.ac.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Molteni joined [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]]{{when|date=November 2018}} as a [[postdoctoral research]] fellow, working on crystalline [[glucose]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Molteni|first1=C.|last2=Parrinello|first2=M.|date=1997|title=Condensed matter effects on the structure of crystalline glucose|bibcode=1997CPL...275..409M|journal=Chemical Physics Letters|language=en|volume=275|issue=3–4|pages=409–413|doi=10.1016/S0009-2614(97)00701-X|issn=0009-2614}}</ref> She used the [[Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics]] method to study glucose.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mrs.org/fall1997/symposium-k|title=Symposium K {{!}} 1995 MRS Fall Meeting {{!}} Boston|website=mrs.org|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref>

Molteni joined the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1999 as an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC) Advanced [[Research Fellow]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=epsrc>{{Cite web |url=https://gtr.ukri.org/person/05964C65-5B85-4286-AC4E-29CBA016D013 |title=GTR |access-date=2018-11-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108065442/https://gtr.ukri.org/person/05964C65-5B85-4286-AC4E-29CBA016D013 |archive-date=2018-11-08 }}</ref> She was a [[fellow]] at [[New Hall, Cambridge|New Hall, (now Murray Edwards College)]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kcl.ac.uk/nms/depts/physics/people/academicstaff/molteni|title=King's College London - Professor Carla Molteni|website=www.kcl.ac.uk|access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> [[New Hall, Cambridge|Cambridge]].

In 2003 Molteni was appointed a professor of soft matter physics at [[King's College London]].<ref name=":1" /> Molteni is a member of the [[Thomas Young Centre]] and [[London Centre for Nanotechnology]].<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://www.thomasyoungcentre.org/people/36/dr-carla-molteni/|title=DR CARLA MOLTENI: Thomas Young Centre|website=thomasyoungcentre.org|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref> She uses [[density functional theory]] and classical methods to understand systems such as [[grain boundaries]], [[liquid crystal]]s, polymers and proteins.<ref name=":2" /> She studied polyamorphism in nanocrystals of silicon.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Molteni|first1=Carla|last2=Martonák|first2=Roman|date=2005|title=Polyamorphism in silicon nanocrystals under pressure|journal=ChemPhysChem|volume=6|issue=9|pages=1765–1768|doi=10.1002/cphc.200400589|issn=1439-4235|pmid=16086341}}</ref> Her group have used computational methods to evaluate the interactions of [[green tea]] with [[cardiac muscle]] and the growth of [[Ice Ih|hexagonal ice]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Botten|first1=Dominic|last2=Fugallo|first2=Giorgia|last3=Fraternali|first3=Franca|last4=Molteni|first4=Carla|date=2013|title=A Computational Exploration of the Interactions of the Green Tea Polyphenol (–)-Epigallocatechin 3-Gallate with Cardiac Muscle Troponin C|journal=PLOS ONE|language=en|volume=8|issue=7|article-number=e70556|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0070556|issn=1932-6203|pmc=3726641|pmid=23923004|bibcode=2013PLoSO...870556B|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Maxwell|first1=Fulford|last2=Matteo|first2=Salvalaglio|last3=Michele|first3=Parrinello|last4=Carla|first4=Molteni|date=2016|title=A Computational Study of the Growth of Hexagonal Ice|journal=APS March Meeting Abstracts|volume=2016|pages=M1.182|language=en|bibcode=2016APS..MAR.M1182F}}</ref> They identified the excited states of biological [[chromophore]]s using many-body perturbation theory.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ma|first1=Yuchen|last2=Rohlfing|first2=Michael|last3=Molteni|first3=Carla|date=2009|title=Excited states of biological chromophores studied using many-body perturbation theory: Effects of resonant-antiresonant coupling and dynamical screening|journal=Physical Review B|volume=80|issue=24|article-number=241405|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.80.241405|bibcode=2009PhRvB..80x1405M}}</ref><ref name="MaRohlfing2010"/> She studied the pressure-induced deformations of nanomaterials and how this impacted their optoelectronic properties.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Corsini|first1=Niccolò R. C.|last2=Hine|first2=Nicholas D. M.|last3=Haynes|first3=Peter D.|last4=Molteni|first4=Carla|date=2017|title=Unravelling the Roles of Size, Ligands, and Pressure in the Piezochromic Properties of CdS Nanocrystals|journal=Nano Letters|language=EN|volume=17|issue=2|pages=1042–1048|doi=10.1021/acs.nanolett.6b04461|issn=1530-6984|pmid= 28128961|bibcode=2017NanoL..17.1042C|doi-access=free|hdl=10044/1/44203|hdl-access=free}}</ref> Understanding [[Piezochromism|piezochromic]] effects is important to determine the potential of a material for applications such as stress sensors.<ref name=":3" />

In 2018 she awarded the ''Italy Made Me'' prizes for young Italian researchers in the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://amblondra.esteri.it/ambasciata_londra/en/ambasciata/ufficio-stampa/news/assegnazione-dei-premi-italy-made.html|title=The 2018 Italy Made Me awards for young Italian researchers in the UK|website=amblondra.esteri.it|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref> She serves on the board of directors of the Association of Italian Scientists in the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aisuk.org/testimonials/|title=About us|website=AISUK|language=en-US|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref> She has taken part in [[Pint of Science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pintofscience.co.uk/event/nature-at-the-nanoscale|title=Nature at the Nanoscale|website=Pint of Science|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-11-07}}</ref>
